title: Expression Analysis of Cell Lines in CCLE
author: Keita Fukuyama
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq5vmy66

steps.title: Download and preprocess datasets
steps.instruction: Download the following files: mRNA expression data (CCLE_Expression.Arrays_2013-03-18.tar.gz) and annotation file (CCLE_Expression.Arrays.sif_2012-10-18.txt) from the CCLE portal (https://portals.broadinstitute.org/ccle); COSMIC data from the ENBL‑EBI website (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/arrayexpress/files/E-MTAB-3610/); microarray CEL files (to be normalized later); RNA‑seq data and annotation from the NCI site (ftp://caftpd.nci.nih.gov/pub/OCG-DCC/CTD2/TGen/CCLE_RNA-seq_Analysis/); TCGA HCC RNA‑seq normalized TPM file (http://gdac.broadinstitute.org/runs/stddata__2016_01_28/data/LIHC/20160128/gdac.broadinstitute.org_LIHC.Merge_rnaseqv2__illuminahiseq_rnaseqv2__unc_edu__Level_3__RSEM_genes_normalized__data.Level_3.2016012800.0.0.tar.gz), raw count file (http://gdac.broadinstitute.org/runs/stddata__2016_01_28/data/LIHC/20160128/gdac.broadinstitute.org_LIHC.Merge_rnaseqv2__illuminahiseq_rnaseqv2__unc_edu__Level_3__RSEM_genes__data.Level_3.2016012800.0.0.tar.gz), and clinical annotation file (http://gdac.broadinstitute.org/runs/stddata__2016_01_28/data/LIHC/20160128/gdac.broadinstitute.org_LIHC.Clinical_Pick_Tier1.Level_4.2016012800.0.0.tar.gz) from the Broad Institute website; additional TCGA clinical data from the GDC portal (https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/repository, S1 Table); and primary cell expression data (GSE49910) from NCBI GEO (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gds/?term=GSE49910[Accession]).

substeps.instruction: Download CCLE expression tarball and annotation file.
Download NCI RNA‑seq and annotation files.
Download TCGA normalized TPM, raw counts, and clinical files.
Download extra TCGA clinical data from GDC.

steps.title: Normalize microarray data
steps.instruction: Apply MAS5 or RMA normalization to all downloaded microarray CEL files, then convert the resulting signal intensities to log2 scale for each probe set ID.

steps.title: Hierarchical clustering of expression
steps.instruction: Perform unsupervised hierarchical clustering on the mRNA expression matrices of cancer cell lines, HCC samples, and primary cells using Spearman correlation distance and either average linkage or Ward’s method; upload the analysis code to GitHub (https://github.com/fk506cni/cell_line_comparison/tree/master/analysis/77GEarray_re).

steps.title: Identify differentially expressed genes
steps.instruction: Using the Bioconductor limma package, compute moderated t‑statistics with the eBayes function, obtain corrected p‑values and Benjamini‑Hochberg q‑values for each probe set ID, and define DEGs as probe set IDs with q‑value < 0.0001.

steps.title: Classify DEGs into cluster‑specific genes
steps.instruction: Calculate the log2 average expression of each DEG in the two liver‑cancer cell‑line clusters; label genes with higher expression in cluster A as “A genes” and those higher in cluster B as “B genes”.

steps.title: PCA and discriminant analysis
steps.instruction: Run principal component analysis on the DEG matrix to assess separation of clusters A and B; then perform discriminant analysis of the principal components using the adegenet R package to evaluate cluster validity.

steps.title: Compare DEGs with TCGA RNA‑seq
steps.instruction: For TCGA HCC RNA‑seq data, transform TPM values as log2(TPM + 1); compute the fold change of each gene between the two clusters; subtract the average expression between clusters and sort genes by the resulting fold‑change values.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of clinical data
steps.instruction: Assess the weight of surgical specimens between clusters with the Brunner‑Munzel test; evaluate the operating‑procedure categories with Fisher’s exact test; fit a Cox proportional‑hazards model and perform a log‑rank test for survival; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.

steps.title: GO enrichment of A and B genes
steps.instruction: Submit the A‑gene and B‑gene lists to DAVID via the Bioconductor RDAVIDWebService package (https://david.ncifcrf.gov/); use the “GOTERM_BP_FAT” annotation and retain terms with Benjamini‑Hochberg‑adjusted p‑value < 0.2; visualize the top ten GO terms with bar plots showing q‑value and number of enriched genes.

steps.title: Map expression to primary cell atlas
steps.instruction: Normalize all CEL files (cell lines and primary cells), integrate them into a single matrix, annotate sample categories from metadata, and visualize the expression patterns with a heatmap.

steps.title: Calculate representative expression vectors
steps.instruction: For each cell type, compute the log2 median of each probe set ID across replicates to generate a representative expression vector (as described in S1 Document).

steps.title: Literature review of liver cell lines
steps.instruction: Search original articles describing the establishment of liver cancer cell lines (references 13‑25); extract patient ages from those studies and compare groups using the Brunner‑Munzel test.

steps.title: Statistical environment setup
steps.instruction: Conduct all analyses and visualizations in RStudio (versions 1.2.5042 and 1.3.959) using R versions 3.4.1, 3.5.3, and 3.6.3 and Bioconductor versions 3.5 and 3.6; deposit all analysis scripts to GitHub (https://github.com/fk506cni/cell_line_comparison); apply Brunner‑Munzel test for continuous variables, Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, and declare significance at p < 0.05.
